title: Three hundred milliseconds of hello
subtitle: The lines an assistant says most, the greeting, the thinking fillers, the short acknowledgements, are pre-rendered per voice at session start and play in under a millisecond, through the same cancellation path as synthesised speech

stats.label: added to session boot to fill the cache
to condition a voice the first time, nothing after
voices held in the bounded conditioning cache

lede: The streaming synthesiser in Building the streaming my speech model did not ship produces its first frame of audio about 300 milliseconds after it is given a sentence, and that figure is flat: eleven characters or two hundred and thirty, the first frame costs the same. For a long answer it is a fine price. For "Hello", "One moment" and "Let me check", which a voice assistant says many times an hour, it is a tax on the words that most need to be instant.
quote: Cached audio has to obey every rule synthesised audio obeys.
evidence: Latency engineering for voice AI: the lines an assistant says most pre-rendered per voice at session start, so they skip the roughly 300 ms a synthesiser takes to its first frame.
Caching design for real-time audio: cached audio held to every rule synthesised audio obeys, filled by about 8 s added to session boot.
Bounded caches: voice conditioning cached for 8 voices, 5.3 s the first time and nothing after.
author: Corey James
